proposals.title: Implement packages/core: branded types, RNG, hash, and CanonicalEncoder
proposals.why_now: Every other FASE-1 deliverable depends on core. The spec mandates that ADR-009 be written and the CanonicalEncoder implemented before any StateHash can exist. All packages are currently stub exports. Nothing in world, domain, application, or the replay CLI can be built correctly until core provides the nominal bigint types, safe-integer Tick, positional RNG, the hash function (a DEFINIR that needs an ADR), and the canonical encoder. This is the single hardest blocker in the current repository.

proposals.title: Electron desktop scaffolding: secure BrowserWindow, simulation worker, minimal UI, and installer
proposals.why_now: The spec explicitly states the installer must exist in FASE-1 in minimal form (§14.6). Electron security configuration (contextIsolation, nodeIntegration off, sandbox, preload allowlist) is required for INV-29, which is a FASE-1 acceptance criterion. Deferring Electron bootstrap risks discovering ABI and module-native issues late. The simulation worker separation from the renderer thread is also a locked architectural requirement. Some scaffolding (BrowserWindow config, preload surface) does not depend on core and can progress in parallel.

repository_assessment.current_state: Monorepo skeleton is complete: all package manifests, strict TypeScript configuration, ESLint determinism-enforcement rules, dependency boundary checker, CI workflow, and tests for lint/boundary/config are in place (TASK-0001 accepted). Every package source is a stub export {}. No production logic, no ADRs, and no invariant tests exist.
repository_assessment.highest_priority_gap: packages/core has zero implementation. It is the direct dependency of every other FASE-1 deliverable. No hash function, RNG, branded types, canonical encoder, or arithmetic helpers exist, blocking world, domain, application, replay CLI, and all invariant tests.

warnings: ADR-009 (CanonicalEncoder) is explicitly required by the spec to be written and the encoder implemented before any StateHash exists. Producing any StateHash before that ADR is recorded is a spec violation, not merely a sequencing preference.

The hash function in ADR-002 is marked DEFINIR. Implementing rand() before registering the algorithm in an ADR would embed an unregistered number with determinism effect, violating §19 and §16 item 7.

ADR-004 rounding enforcement technique is also DEFINIR. The division-without-mode compile/lint error mechanism must be specified in an ADR before domain arithmetic is written, or the invariant has no enforcement.

The spec requires tools/bench to establish calibration ratios and freeze them in FASE-1. These baselines cannot be frozen until core and world exist, so bench work is sequentially blocked but must not be deferred past FASE-1 acceptance.
